subject: Kestrel Labs - reference implementation sign-off & sandbox onboarding
messages:
From: Maggie Zhou <maggie@kestrel-labs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Healey <tom.healey@kestrel-labs.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kestrel reference design + sandbox request

Hi Hannah / Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the hosted vs dedicated routing options and Kestrel is keen to validate a reference implementation that demonstrates:

- End-to-end latency with prefix caching for our 1k token LLM prompts
- Cost delta between quantized vs fp16 for our reranking pipeline
- Failure recovery when a model variant is out of capacity (fallback behavior)

Attached is our current reference architecture (kestrel_ref_arch_v1.pdf) and an initial test matrix (kestrel_test_matrix.xlsx). Can Redwood provision a short-lived sandbox where we can run the matrix (2 dev GPUs, sample dataset, limited ingress)? Ideal window: Jul 6–8.

Also: we need a short checklist for security gating (SOC2 pointers, data retention, audit log access) so our compliance team can pre-check.

Next steps we’d like:
1) Confirm sandbox dates and connectivity model (VPC peering vs temporary token)
2) Agree on test scenarios and success criteria (latency percentiles, cost thresholds)
3) Exchange contact for engineering pairing during tests

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Maggie Zhou
Solutions Architect, Kestrel Labs
maggie@kestrel-labs.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: kestrel_ref_arch_v1.pdf (application/pdf), kestrel_test_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Subject: Re: Kestrel reference design + sandbox request

Hi Maggie —

Thanks for the detailed deck and matrix, this is exactly the level we need. We can absolutely stand up a short sandbox for Jul 6–8 and run the scenarios you outlined. Quick notes:

- Sandbox model: we can provision a VPC-peered sandbox with two P4d-equivalent GPUs and a pre-seeded sample dataset.
- Connectivity: VPC peering preferred for data security; temp token option if you need faster network setup.
- Compliance: we’ll attach the Redwood security checklist and SOC2 pointer doc for your compliance team.

I’ve looped in Jonas (runtime/benchmarks) and Lauren (partner onboarding) — Jonas will own the test orchestration; Lauren will coordinate billing/contract sign-off and any MSA/DocuSign items.

Propose a 30-min sync tomorrow (Jun 30) 10:00–10:30 PT to finalize the sandbox details and checklist. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite. Please confirm who from Kestrel will be on the call (engineer + security contact is helpful).

Action items from Redwood for Jul 6–8 test window:
- Provision VPC-peered sandbox and create onboarding doc (redwood-sandbox-onboarding.md)
- Preload sample dataset and credentials vault entry
- Provide SOC2 excerpt + security checklist for review

Thanks — looking forward to this.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maggie Zhou <maggie@kestrel-labs.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel reference design + sandbox request

Maggie / Hannah —

Quick technical checklist and run notes before tomorrow’s sync. I attached a short Redwood test checklist (redwood-test-checklist.docx) but key points inline: 

1) Model choices & profiles
   - Recommend starting with a 2.7B open-weights variant for reranking and a 7B quantized variant for generation.
   - Use Q4_0-8bit quantization for the 7B to balance quality and cost; record token-quality deltas.

2) Batching and latency
   - Target 95th-percentile < 250ms for single-turn 512-token prompts with continuous batching off for the first run; enable batching for throughput tests.

3) Cache & KV validation
   - Seed prefix cache with 5k examples to test cache hit effectiveness. We’ll measure cache-hit ratio impact on latency/cost.

4) Failure/rollback behavior
   - We’ll simulate model OOM and exercise automatic fallback to smaller variant; verify request tracing preserves correlation IDs.

5) Data safety & logs
   - Audit logs will be retained for 30 days in the sandbox and accessible via the runbook link. Sensitive fields will be redacted in the sample dataset prior to load.

Resource estimate for the three-day run: 2 dev GPUs (P4-equivalent), 1 staging CPU host, 1200 token storage for sample dataset. If Kestrel wants a dedicated cost estimate we can produce an itemized run-cost before tests.

I’ll bring automated scripts to capture latency/cost traces and a short post-test template so we can compare quantization vs fp16.

Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-test-checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
